title.narrative: Climate Finance Access, Absorption and Implementation in the Pacific

description.narrative: Active

The Programme aims to increase PICs resilience and adaptive capacity to climate change and reduce their CO2 emissions in line with National Adaptation Plans and NDC commitments through enhanced capacity and institutional capability to improve access to climate finance and strengthen their absorptive capacity for efficient delivery of impactful climate change programmes.

The United Kingdom and GGGI signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on 11 August 2023 to strengthen institutional capacity to access, absorb and deliver impactful climate finance in the Pacific. The project totalling STG1.8 million to be implemented in 7 PICs (Vanuatu, PNG, Fiji, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Samoa, and Kiribati) was for an initial project term of 1 year (to 31 March 2025). In March 2024, the UK and GGGI signed an Amendment to the MOU extending the project for a further twelve months (to 31 March 2026) with an additional sum of STG1.6m. The program's rapid success in mobilising additional investment funding for PICs including establishment of National Financing Vehicles in various PICs has gained recognition and support by PICs. This has led to the FCDO, despite recent deep cuts to the UK aid program globally, supporting a new phase for the project to March 2027.
